set system host-name [parameter1].explanation: Configure the host name of the device.

parameters.name: hostname
parameters.explanation: The host name of the equipment is used to identify the equipment in the network.

unit [parameter2].explanation: Configure the unit number of the interface.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.explanation: Interface unit numbers that distinguish between multiple logical configurations under the same interface.

family inet address [parameter3]/[parame.explanation: Configure IPv4 addresses for interfaces and subnet masks.

parameters.name: ip-address
parameters.explanation: The IPv4 address assigned to the interface.

family inet address [parameter3].explanation: The command `family inet address [parameter3]` configures an IPv4 address (`[parameter3]`) on an interface in Junos OS.

parameters.name: ip-address
parameters.explanation: The IPv4 address assigned to the interface.

vrrp-group [parameter4].explanation: The command `vrrp-group [parameter4]` configures a Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) group with the specified group identifier `[parameter4]`.

virtual-address [parameter5].explanation: The command `virtual-address [parameter5]` in Junos configures a shared IP address for redundancy protocols like VRRP or clustering, where `[parameter5]` specifies the IP address.

parameters.name: virtual-address
parameters.explanation: Virtual IPv4 address of VRRP team.

priority [parameter5].explanation: The command `priority [parameter5]` sets the priority level for a routing protocol or interface, influencing its preference in route selection or failover scenarios.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.explanation: The higher the value, the higher the VRP Group priority.

preempt hold-time [parameter5].explanation: The command `preempt hold-time [parameter5]` sets a delay (in seconds) before a higher-priority router can preempt a lower-priority router in a VRRP group.

parameters.name: hold-time
parameters.explanation: Grab hold of time, in seconds.

set chassis fpc [parameter1].explanation: Sets the specified parameter for a Flexible PIC Concentrator (FPC) in the Junos chassis, configuring hardware-specific behavior or operational state.

pic [parameter2].explanation: This command configures a Flexible PIC Concentrator (FPC) and its associated Physical Interface Card (PIC) in a Junos device, specifying parameters for hardware settings.

set routing-options static route [parame.explanation: This command configures a static route in Junos, where `[parameter1]` is the destination network and `[parameter2]` is the subnet mask.

set services ds-lite instance [parameter.explanation: The command configures a DS-Lite instance named `[parameter1]`, enabling IPv4 over IPv6 tunneling by associating it with specific address families and interfaces.

id [parameter2].explanation: The command `id [parameter2]` in Junos assigns a unique identifier or name to a specific configuration element, such as a policy, interface, or security zone.

port-range [parameter2].explanation: The `port-range [parameter2]` command in Junos specifies a range of port numbers for a service or application, where `[parameter2]` defines the end port in the range.

service-instance-group [parameter2].explanation: The command `service-instance-group [parameter2]` assigns a service instance group to a specific interface or service set in Junos for traffic processing.

address-group [parameter2].explanation: The command `address-group [parameter2]` creates or references a group of IP addresses in Junos, where `[parameter2]` specifies the group's name or identifier.

group-id [parameter3].explanation: The command `group-id [parameter3]` specifies the identifier for a group, such as a security group or policy group, in Junos configuration.

section [parameter3].explanation: The command `section [parameter3]` in Junos displays only the configuration section related to `[parameter3]`, filtering out other parts of the configuration.

prefix [parameter4]/[parameter5].explanation: The command `prefix [parameter4]/[parameter5]` specifies a network prefix with `[parameter4]` as the IP address and `[parameter5]` as the subnet mask length.

outbound any address-group [parameter2].explanation: The command configures an outbound NAT rule, translating any source IP to an address from the specified address-group `[parameter2]`.

local-ipv6 [parameter2]/[parameter3].explanation: The command `local-ipv6 [parameter2]/[parameter3]` assigns an IPv6 address (`parameter2`) with a specified prefix length (`parameter3`) to a local interface.

remote-ipv6 [parameter2]/[parameter3].explanation: The command `remote-ipv6 [parameter2]/[parameter3]` specifies the IPv6 address (`parameter2`) and prefix length (`parameter3`) for a remote endpoint in a Junos configuration.

alg enable [parameter2].explanation: The command `alg enable [parameter2]` in Junos enables Application Layer Gateway (ALG) for a specific protocol or service specified by `[parameter2]`.

filter mode [parameter2].explanation: The command `filter mode [parameter2]` in Junos sets the filtering mode for a specific interface or protocol, where `[parameter2]` specifies the desired mode (e.g., `exact`, `prefix`).
